text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a tenant with a sudden 3x token bill yesterday. Looks correlated with the console "Prefer v2 by default" toggle flip. Can we confirm routing switch and quota mapping?
Maria: ugh, that banner got flipped in a micro-release? Which tenant? any traces? :eyes:
Alex: tenant `acme-inc` — logs show X-Redwood-Client-Version header absent, console flag used to opt them into default v2. Routing service treated them as v2 and applied v2 per-route quota buckets (which are smaller) so they hit overage fast.
Chris: if header absent we fall back to account-level default. The console toggle changed the default at account scope, which should be fine, but quota-shape for v2 was indeed lower for that tenant. We should have telemetry to catch per-tenant per-version quota jumps.
Jordan: small note — our current quota key is `tenant_id + route + version_tag` but console default flip only sets `account.default_version` and not an explicit `version_tag` on existing routes. So routing matched v2 variant (since default), but quota migration wasn't coordinated.
Priya: proposed immediate mitigation: add a migration shim that keeps quota keys bound to the route's previous `pinned_version` unless a route-level opt-in flag is set. Short-term we can auto-add `pinned_version=v1` metadata for existing routes when flipping account default.
Maria: agree. Also adding a telemetry alert: detect >50% of traffic for a tenant switching version within 1h combined with >20% increase in token spend. PromQL sketch: `sum by(tenant,version) (rate(tokens_used[5m])) / sum by(tenant) (rate(tokens_used[5m])) > 0.5` and `increase(cost_total[1h]) > 0.2 * increase(cost_total[24h])`
Chris: that PromQL looks fine. Logging team: can we emit an explicit audit event on console toggles that includes impacted route list and pre/post quota-buckets? That'll help backfill.
deploy-bot: feature-flag created: `route.quota_shim_on_default_flip` (owner: @Priya).
Alex: thanks. For a quick containment, can we add a tenant-level emergency override that forces routing to v1 for 24h? This should be a console button and a token-level header shim.
Jordan: add `X-Redwood-Force-Version: v1` support in routing proxy and make it honored before account default. Will also add a soft-logging marker so we can track overrides.
Priya: I'll work on the shim and the feature-flag rollout. Plan: 1) enable `route.quota_shim_on_default_flip` for all accounts, 2) add override button in console + SDK helper, 3) telemetry alert, 4) migration job to set `pinned_version` for routes created before toggle. Start a canary rollout to 5% of accounts.
Maria: UX suggestion — make the console toggle show an explicit alert that this will mutate per-route quotas and show a count of affected routes. Right now it says "change default" with no hint. That small affordance would've prevented this.
Chris: agree, let's add a modal and require a confirmation checkbox. Also add an API response header `X-Redwood-Route-Version: v2` when routing to v2 for visibility.
Alex: action items: Priya -> shim + flag + canary (PR pls), Jordan -> force-header support + logging, Maria -> telemetry alert + console modal copy, Chris -> response header change + docs note. I'll open a Jira and link everything.
Priya: quick Q — do we want the migration job to be automatic or require opt-in per tenant? I think automatic with a 7-day rollback window and notification to tenant admins.
Maria: automatic but email + console notification is needed. Also add a metric `quota_migration_count{tenant}`.
Chris: can ops throttle the migration so we don't overload quota service? maybe 100 tenants/min.
Jordan: noted. We'll add backpressure and per-account pacing.
Alex: Thanks team. If anyone sees another unexplained billing spike, ping #billing-alerts and me directly. I'll paste the Jira in this thread when created. :thumbsup:
_notes: This thread records an eng-platform discussion about a console default-version toggle that unintentionally migrated tenants to v2 routing without coordinating quota keys, causing billing spikes. The thread includes an immediate mitigation plan, telemetry, UX changes, and a feature-flagged rollout. Messages are short and Slack-style with inline code and a PromQL sketch.
